what: Fortis is a North American regulated utility. It owns electricity and gas utilities in Canada, the Caribbean and the United States, including ITC, the largest independent electricity transmission company in the US.
customers: About 3.5 million electricity and gas customers across Canada, the United States and the Caribbean.
money: federally regulated electricity transmission in the Midwest
utilities in Arizona and the Midwest
British Columbia, Alberta, Ontario and Atlantic Canada
moat: Regulated monopolies in many separate jurisdictions, so no single regulator can damage the whole company, with transmission assets earning federally set returns.
risks: Return on invested capital of about 5%, normal for a regulated utility
Rate decisions across many jurisdictions each affect a slice of earnings
Analyst coverage here is thin and the target implies downside
opportunities: Revenue grew about 11% last year with a 29% operating margin
A dividend increased every year for more than fifty years
Transmission investment grows as renewable generation is connected
watch: Rate base growth and regulatory decisions at ITC.
